description: Technical approver vs contract signer; a quotes-threshold amount; an internal review meeting.

turns.text: Can you walk me through how approvals work for a tool like this?
Sure. Anil Gupta owns the technical approval, so security review, architecture, all of that goes through him.
The contract is signed by our CFO, Daniel Kim. He signs every software agreement.
Got it. Any purchasing rules I should know about?
Anything over twenty-five thousand needs three competing quotes, so expect our procurement folks to ask for that.
Noted. Are you meeting internally about this soon?
We have our architecture review board on Wednesday. I'll share notes with you after.

evidence.quote: Anything over twenty-five thousand needs three competing quotes

budget.rationale: 25K is a purchasing threshold, not an approved budget (§2.1). No budget is stated.

evidence.quote: The contract is signed by our CFO, Daniel Kim. He signs every software agreement.

decisionMaker.rationale: Contract signature = final purchase authority (§2.2 'Distinct approval types'). Anil's technical approval is not final.

evidence.quote: We have our architecture review board on Wednesday.

nextMeeting.rationale: An internal customer meeting the seller won't attend is not a nextMeeting (§2.3).

notes: Intended difficulty: moderate. Distractors: budget, decisionMaker, meeting. Generated by Claude for the dev split; labels are drafts pending owner review. Anil (technical approver) is an INDIRECT claim that does not compete with the DIRECT contract signer (LABELING_GUIDE v1.1 §4 step 4).
